name: common_upscale and LatentUpscale / LatentUpscaleBy
plain: The shared resize used nearly everywhere. It flattens 5D video into 4D, optionally centre-crops to the target aspect, calls bislerp, lanczos, or torch interpolate, then restores the 5D shape. LatentUpscale takes pixel sizes and divides by 8 with a hard-coded factor of 8; LatentUpscaleBy multiplies latent size directly. No variance compensation for any mode.
math:
crop center: trim round((old − old·(new_aspect/old_aspect))/2) from the wider axis.
mode bislerp → bislerp; lanczos → PIL lanczos; else F.interpolate(mode).
LatentUpscale: w//8, h//8 with min 64 px. If one is 0 the other is derived from aspect.
LatentUpscale node choices: nearest-exact, bilinear, area, bicubic, bislerp. Lanczos is not offered on these two nodes.
label: from code
surprise: LatentUpscale hard-codes //8 (nodes.py:1375), so on a 16x-downscale or non-8x VAE the pixel size widgets do not mean pixels.

audit.note: utils.py:1142-1157: 5D input is flattened to 4D before the centre crop, not after; shape is restored after resizing (1168-1172).
